rationale: Set A wins because it understands the difference between a story REI can pitch and a hard question REI must be ready to answer. A correctly refuses "Record dividend lands amid union drives — what REI owes its workers vs its members" as an own-goal, while B promotes "A record member payout while several stores see union drives: the co-op's two stories at once" into a target angle. That may be real journalism, but as company-side strategy it hands a labor reporter the knife and calls it outreach.
gaps_in_A: "The prevailing belief: resale and repair cannibalize new-product sales" is plausible, but it is not in the supplied facts; A handles it as a thesis, but it still needs external proof before pitching.
"The retailer paying its owners a record dividend is the one betting on used gear" risks implying a stronger connection between the dividend and resale strategy than the update proves.
The member-service angle is useful, but it needs hard examples fast; without "what a used tent or pair of boots fetches," it becomes polite brochure copy.
gaps_in_B: "A record member payout while several stores see union drives: the co-op's two stories at once" is the wrong accepted angle for REI to pitch; it belongs in prep, not outbound media strategy.
"ongoing unionization activity" overstates the supplied fact, which only says REI "has faced unionization activity at several stores." Current status is missing.
"The contrarian angle is your sharpest and your riskiest" mistakes danger for strategy. Sharp is not the same as pitchable.
B misses the cleaner consumer-service angle: members can now trade in gear and get repairs at any store. That is more usable than turning the campaign into a labor fight.
